237	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- AST checks
238	def _touches(node: ast.AST, lines: set[int]) -> bool:
239	    start = getattr(node, "lineno", 0)
240	    end = getattr(node, "end_lineno", start) or start
241	    return any(start <= n <= end for n in lines)
242	
243	
244	def _is_trivial(body: list[ast.stmt]) -> bool:
245	    """Only pass, `...` or `raise NotImplementedError`, after an optional docstring."""
246	    stmts = body[1:] if body and _is_docstring(body[0]) else body
247	    return all(_is_placeholder(s) for s in stmts)
248	
249	
250	def _task_stub(body: list[ast.stmt]) -> str | None:
251	    """The task an interface stub names: a body that is only `raise NotImplementedError("M1-T05")`."""
252	    stmts = body[1:] if body and _is_docstring(body[0]) else body
253	    if len(stmts) != 1 or not isinstance(stmts[0], ast.Raise):
254	        return None
255	    exc = stmts[0].exc
256	    if not (isinstance(exc, ast.Call) and _name(exc.func) == "NotImplementedError"):
257	        return None
258	    arg = exc.args[0] if len(exc.args) == 1 and not exc.keywords else None
259	    if (
260	        isinstance(arg, ast.Constant)
261	        and isinstance(arg.value, str)
262	        and TASK_ID.fullmatch(arg.value)
263	    ):
264	        return arg.value
265	    return None
266	
267	
268	def _is_docstring(stmt: ast.stmt) -> bool:
269	    return (
270	        isinstance(stmt, ast.Expr)
271	        and isinstance(stmt.value, ast.Constant)
272	        and isinstance(stmt.value.value, str)
273	    )
274	
275	
276	def _is_placeholder(stmt: ast.stmt) -> bool:
277	    if isinstance(stmt, ast.Pass):
278	        return True
279	    if isinstance(stmt, ast.Expr) and isinstance(stmt.value, ast.Constant):
280	        return stmt.value.value is Ellipsis
281	    if isinstance(stmt, ast.Raise) and stmt.exc is not None:
282	        exc = stmt.exc.func if isinstance(stmt.exc, ast.Call) else stmt.exc
283	        return _name(exc) == "NotImplementedError"
284	    return False
285	
286	
287	def _name(node: ast.AST) -> str | None:
288	    if isinstance(node, ast.Name):
289	        return node.id
290	    if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute):
291	        return node.attr
292	    if isinstance(node, ast.Call):
293	        return _name(node.func)
294	    return None
295	
296	
297	def _exempt_functions(tree: ast.Module) -> set[ast.AST]:
298	    """Abstract methods, overloads and Protocol members may have placeholder bodies."""
299	    exempt: set[ast.AST] = set()
300	    for node in ast.walk(tree):
301	        if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
302	            if {_name(d) for d in node.decorator_list} & EXEMPT_DECORATORS:
303	                exempt.add(node)
304	        elif isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef) and "Protocol" in {_name(b) for b in node.bases}:
305	            exempt.update(
306	                n for n in node.body if isinstance(n, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef))
307	            )
308	    return exempt
309	
310	
311	def _in_folder(name: str | None, folder: str) -> bool:
312	    return name is not None and (name == folder or name.startswith(f"{folder}."))
313	
314	
315	def _mentions(node: ast.AST, word: re.Pattern[str]) -> bool:
316	    return any(
317	        isinstance(n, ast.Constant) and isinstance(n.value, str) and word.search(n.value)
318	        for n in ast.walk(node)
319	    )
320	
321	
322	def _is_sys_path(node: ast.AST) -> bool:
323	    return (
324	        isinstance(node, ast.Attribute)
325	        and node.attr == "path"
326	        and isinstance(node.value, ast.Name)
327	        and node.value.id == "sys"
328	    )
329	
330	
331	def _imported_modules(node: ast.AST) -> list[str | None]:
332	    """Absolute module names an import statement or an import_module call brings in."""
333	    if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
334	        return [alias.name for alias in node.names]
335	    if isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
336	        return [node.module] if node.level == 0 else []
337	    if isinstance(node, ast.Call) and _name(node.func) in {"import_module", "__import__"}:
338	        first = node.args[0] if node.args else None
339	        if isinstance(first, ast.Constant) and isinstance(first.value, str):
340	            return [first.value]
341	    return []
342	
343	
344	def _changes_sys_path(node: ast.AST) -> bool:
345	    """sys.path.insert/append/extend, site.addsitedir, or an assignment to sys.path."""
346	    if isinstance(node, ast.Call) and isinstance(node.func, ast.Attribute):
347	        func = node.func
348	        return func.attr == "addsitedir" or (
349	            func.attr in SYS_PATH_CALLS and _is_sys_path(func.value)
350	        )
351	    if isinstance(node, ast.Assign):
352	        return any(_is_sys_path(target) for target in node.targets)
353	    if isinstance(node, ast.AugAssign):
354	        return _is_sys_path(node.target)
355	    return False
356	
357	
358	def _outside_finding(path: str, node: ast.AST) -> Finding | None:
359	    """CR-08: an import from references/ or probes/, or either folder added to sys.path."""
360	    line = getattr(node, "lineno", 0)
361	    for folder, word in OUTSIDE.items():
362	        if any(_in_folder(name, folder) for name in _imported_modules(node)):
363	            return Finding(f"{folder}-import", path, line, f"import from {folder}/")
364	        if _changes_sys_path(node) and _mentions(node, word):
365	            return Finding(f"{folder}-path", path, line, f"{folder}/ added to sys.path")
366	    return None
367	
368	
369	def _asserts(func: ast.AST) -> bool:
370	    for node in ast.walk(func):
371	        if isinstance(node, ast.Assert):
372	            return True
373	        name = _name(node) if isinstance(node, ast.Call) else None
374	        if name and (
375	            name.startswith("assert") or name in {"raises", "warns", "deprecated_call", "fail"}
376	        ):
377	            return True
378	    return False
379	
380	
381	def ast_findings(path: str, lines: set[int]) -> list[Finding]:
382	    try:
383	        tree = ast.parse(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
384	    except (SyntaxError, UnicodeDecodeError, OSError):
385	        return []  # ruff reports syntax errors; a deleted file has nothing to check
386	    exempt, test = _exempt_functions(tree), is_test_file(path)
387	    found: list[Finding] = []
388	    for node in ast.walk(tree):
389	        if not _touches(node, lines):
390	            continue
391	        if outside := _outside_finding(path, node):
392	            found.append(outside)
393	        if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
394	            if (
395	                node not in exempt
396	                and not path.endswith(".pyi")
397	                and _is_trivial(node.body)
398	                and not _task_stub(node.body)
399	            ):
400	                found.append(
401	                    Finding("stub", path, node.lineno, f"`{node.name}` has a placeholder body")
402	                )
403	            if test and node.name.startswith("test") and not _asserts(node):
404	                found.append(
405	                    Finding(
406	                        "test-without-assertion",
407	                        path,
408	                        node.lineno,
409	                        f"`{node.name}` asserts nothing",
410	                    )
411	                )
412	        elif isinstance(node, ast.ExceptHandler) and _is_trivial(node.body):
413	            if (None if node.type is None else _name(node.type)) in TRIVIAL_EXCEPT:
414	                found.append(
415	                    Finding("swallowed-exception", path, node.lineno, "exception swallowed")
416	                )
417	    return found
418

420	def open_tasks() -> set[str]:
421	    """Task IDs with an unchecked line in tasks/todo.md (none when there is no todo)."""
422	    path = Path("tasks/todo.md")
423	    return set(OPEN_TASK.findall(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))) if path.is_file() else set()

426	def task_stub_findings(paths: list[str], at_exit: bool) -> list[Finding]:
427	    """Interface stubs anywhere in the project's code: each must name an open task, and at the
428	    milestone exit none may be left. Not diff-scoped: the stub was written by an earlier task."""
429	    open_ids, found = open_tasks(), []
430	    for path in paths:
431	        if not is_python(path) or is_test_file(path) or not Path(path).is_file():
432	            continue
433	        try:
434	            tree = ast.parse(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
435	        except (SyntaxError, UnicodeDecodeError, OSError):
436	            continue
437	        for node in ast.walk(tree):
438	            if not isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
439	                continue
440	            if not (task := _task_stub(node.body)):
441	                continue
442	            if at_exit:
443	                found.append(
444	                    Finding(
445	                        "stub-left",
446	                        path,
447	                        node.lineno,
448	                        f"`{node.name}` is still the stub for {task}",
449	                    )
450	                )
451	            elif task not in open_ids:
452	                found.append(
453	                    Finding(
454	                        "stub-task",
455	                        path,
456	                        node.lineno,
457	                        f"`{node.name}` is a stub naming {task}, which is not open in tasks/todo.md",
458	                    )
459	                )
460	    return found

463	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the bar: tool config
464	MAX_KEYS = (
465	    "tool.ruff.lint.mccabe.max-complexity",
466	    "tool.size_limits.max_module_lines",
467	    "tool.size_limits.max_function_lines",
468	    "tool.vulture.min_confidence",
469	    "tool.pylint.similarities.min-similarity-lines",
470	)
471	MIN_KEYS = ("tool.coverage.report.fail_under", "tool.size_limits.min_module_lines")
472	TRUE_KEYS = ("tool.mypy.strict", "tool.pytest.ini_options.xfail_strict")
473	OFF_KEYS = ("tool.pylint.main.exit-zero",)  # turning one on silences a check
474	NO_SHRINK = ("tool.ruff.lint.select", "tool.ruff.lint.extend-select")
475	NO_GROW = (
476	    "tool.ruff.lint.ignore", "tool.ruff.lint.extend-ignore", "tool.ruff.exclude",
477	    "tool.ruff.extend-exclude", "tool.ruff.lint.exclude", "tool.deptry.exclude",
478	    "tool.deptry.extend_exclude", "tool.deptry.ignore", "tool.vulture.ignore_names",
479	    "tool.vulture.exclude", "tool.mypy.exclude", "tool.pylint.main.ignore-paths",
480	    "tool.pylint.main.ignore", "tool.pylint.main.ignore-patterns",
481	)  # fmt: skip
482	# Excluding the references or probes folder is not a loosening: neither is project code (CR-08).
483	OUTSIDE_EXCLUDE = re.compile(r"\^?(references|probes)/?\*{0,2}")
484	NO_GROW_TABLES = ("tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores", "tool.deptry.per_rule_ignores")
485	MUST_MATCH = ("tool.importlinter", "tool.mypy.overrides", "tool.pyright")
486	STRICT_FLAGS = ("--strict-markers", "--strict-config")
487	
488	
489	def _get(data: dict[str, Any], dotted: str) -> Any:
490	    for key in dotted.split("."):
491	        if not isinstance(data, dict) or key not in data:
492	            return None
493	        data = data[key]
494	    return data
495	
496	
497	def _as_set(value: Any) -> set[str]:
498	    if isinstance(value, str):
499	        return {value}
500	    return {str(v) for v in value} if isinstance(value, list) else set()
501	
502	
503	def _limit_findings(old: dict[str, Any], new: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
504	    pylint = _get(old, "tool.ruff.lint.pylint") or {}
505	    maxes = [*MAX_KEYS, *(f"tool.ruff.lint.pylint.{k}" for k in pylint)]
506	    out = [
507	        f"{k}: {_get(old, k)} -> {_get(new, k)}"
508	        for k in maxes
509	        if _loosened(_get(old, k), _get(new, k), +1)
510	    ]
511	    out += [
512	        f"{k}: {_get(old, k)} -> {_get(new, k)}"
513	        for k in MIN_KEYS
514	        if _loosened(_get(old, k), _get(new, k), -1)
515	    ]
516	    out += [
517	        f"{k} turned off" for k in TRUE_KEYS if _get(old, k) is True and _get(new, k) is not True
518	    ]
519	    out += [f"{k} turned on" for k in OFF_KEYS if _get(new, k) is True and _get(old, k) is not True]
520	    return out
521	
522	
523	def _loosened(was: Any, now: Any, direction: int) -> bool:
524	    if not isinstance(was, (int, float)):
525	        return False
526	    if not isinstance(now, (int, float)):
527	        return True  # a limit that disappeared
528	    return (now - was) * direction > 0
529	
530	
531	def _list_findings(old: dict[str, Any], new: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
532	    out = [f"{k} lost {sorted(_as_set(_get(old, k)) - _as_set(_get(new, k)))}" for k in NO_SHRINK]
533	    for k in NO_GROW:
534	        gained = _as_set(_get(new, k)) - _as_set(_get(old, k))
535	        out.append(f"{k} gained {sorted(g for g in gained if not OUTSIDE_EXCLUDE.fullmatch(g))}")
536	    for table in NO_GROW_TABLES:
537	        was, now = _get(old, table) or {}, _get(new, table) or {}
538	        out += [
539	            f"{table}.{key} gained {sorted(_as_set(codes) - _as_set(was.get(key)))}"
540	            for key, codes in now.items()
541	            if _as_set(codes) - _as_set(was.get(key))
542	        ]
543	    flags = _as_set((_get(new, "tool.pytest.ini_options.addopts") or "").split())
544	    out += [
545	        f"pytest addopts dropped {f}"
546	        for f in STRICT_FLAGS
547	        if f in str(_get(old, "tool.pytest.ini_options.addopts")) and f not in flags
548	    ]
549	    out += [
550	        f"{k} changed (boundaries and type config change only through build-setup)"
551	        for k in MUST_MATCH
552	        if _get(old, k) != _get(new, k)
553	    ]
554	    return [o for o in out if not o.endswith("[]")]
555	
556	
557	def config_findings(old_pyproject: Path, diff: Diff) -> list[Finding]:
558	    found = [
559	        Finding("bar-loosened", p, 0, "new tool config file overrides pyproject.toml")
560	        for p in diff.added
561	        if Path(p).name in CONFIG_FILES and not p.startswith("scripts/")
562	    ]
563	    old_text = old_pyproject.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if old_pyproject.is_file() else ""
564	    if not old_text or not Path("pyproject.toml").is_file():
565	        return found
566	    try:
567	        old, new = (
568	            tomllib.loads(old_text),
569	            tomllib.loads(Path("pyproject.toml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")),
570	        )
571	    except tomllib.TOMLDecodeError as exc:
572	        return [*found, Finding("bar-loosened", "pyproject.toml", 0, f"cannot parse: {exc}")]
573	    changes = _limit_findings(old, new) + _list_findings(old, new)
574	    return found + [Finding("bar-loosened", "pyproject.toml", 0, c) for c in changes]
575

577	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------- CONSTRAINTS.md
578	RULE_REF = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:-\s*\*\*(CR-\d+)\*\*|\|\s*(CR-\d+)\s*\|)")
579	
580	
581	def _section(lines: list[str], title: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
582	    """1-based line range of a `## title` section, or (0, -1)."""
583	    start = next((i for i, t in enumerate(lines, 1) if t.strip().lower() == f"## {title}"), 0)
584	    if not start:
585	        return 0, -1
586	    end = next(
587	        (i - 1 for i, t in enumerate(lines, 1) if i > start and t.startswith("## ")), len(lines)
588	    )
589	    return start, end
590	
591	
592	def _table_rows(lines: list[str], start: int, end: int) -> list[tuple[int, list[str]]]:
593	    rows = []
594	    for n in range(start + 1, end + 1):
595	        text = lines[n - 1].strip()
596	        if not text.startswith("|"):
597	            continue
598	        cells = [c.strip() for c in text.strip("|").split("|")]
599	        if cells and cells[0] not in {"", "ID"} and not set(cells[0]) <= set("-: "):
600	            rows.append((n, cells))
601	    return rows
602	
603	
604	def constraints_findings(diff: Diff) -> list[Finding]:
605	    path = "CONSTRAINTS.md"
606	    if path not in diff.added and path not in diff.removed:
607	        return []
608	    still = {
609	        m.group(1) or m.group(2) for _, t in diff.added.get(path, []) if (m := RULE_REF.match(t))
610	    }
611	    gone = {
612	        m.group(1) or m.group(2) for t in diff.removed.get(path, []) if (m := RULE_REF.match(t))
613	    }
614	    found = [Finding("rule-removed", path, 0, f"{rule} removed") for rule in sorted(gone - still)]
615	    lines = Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if Path(path).is_file() else []
616	    start, end = _section(lines, "exceptions")
617	    new_rows = diff.added_lines(path)
618	    found += [
619	        Finding("new-exception", path, n, f"new exception {cells[0]} needs the user's yes")
620	        for n, cells in _table_rows(lines, start, end)
621	        if n in new_rows
622	    ]
623	    return found
624	
625	
626	def load_exceptions(today: date) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
627	    """(rule cell, path glob) for each unexpired row in CONSTRAINTS.md's Exceptions table."""
628	    path = Path("CONSTRAINTS.md")
629	    if not path.is_file():
630	        return []
631	    lines = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
632	    allowed = []
633	    for _, cells in _table_rows(lines, *_section(lines, "exceptions")):
634	        if len(cells) < 6:
635	            continue
636	        expires = re.match(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", cells[5])
637	        if expires and date.fromisoformat(expires[0]) < today:
638	            continue
639	        allowed.append((cells[1], cells[2].strip("`")))
640	    return allowed
641	
642	
643	def is_excepted(finding: Finding, allowed: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> bool:
644	    rule_id = RULE_IDS.get(finding.rule)
645	    return bool(rule_id) and any(
646	        rule_id in rule and fnmatch.fnmatch(finding.path, glob) for rule, glob in allowed
647	    )
648	
649	
650	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- main
651	def run(
652	    diff: Diff, old_pyproject: Path, python_files: list[str] | None = None, at_exit: bool = False
653	) -> list[Finding]:
654	    found = line_findings(diff) + test_file_findings(diff)
655	    found += task_stub_findings(python_files or [], at_exit)
656	    for path in diff.added:
657	        if is_python(path):
658	            found += ast_findings(path, diff.added_lines(path))
659	    found += config_findings(old_pyproject, diff) + constraints_findings(diff)
660	    allowed = load_exceptions(datetime.now(tz=UTC).date())
661	    return [f for f in found if not is_excepted(f, allowed)]
662	
663	
664	def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
665	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
666	    parser.add_argument("--diff", type=Path, required=True)
667	    parser.add_argument("--untracked", type=Path, required=True)
668	    parser.add_argument("--old-pyproject", type=Path, required=True)
669	    parser.add_argument(
670	        "--python", type=Path, help="every Python file in the project, one per line"
671	    )
672	    parser.add_argument(
673	        "--exit", action="store_true", help="the milestone exit: no stub may be left"
674	    )
675	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
676	    diff = parse_diff(args.diff.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))
677	    add_untracked(diff, args.untracked.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines())
678	    python_files = args.python.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if args.python else []
679	    findings = run(diff, args.old_pyproject, python_files, args.exit)
680	    if not findings:
681	        print("floor_guard: clean", file=sys.stderr)
682	        return 0
683	    print("\n".join(str(f) for f in sorted(findings)))
684	    print(
685	        f"floor_guard: {len(findings)} floor violation(s). Fix the code; a real exception goes "
686	        "through build-setup (Revise) and the Exceptions table in CONSTRAINTS.md.",
687	        file=sys.stderr,
688	    )
689	    return 1
690	
691	
692	if __name__ == "__main__":
693	    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

"""The shared contract types: world and policy protocols, settings, seed sets and outputs."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Mapping
from dataclasses import dataclass, fields
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Literal, Protocol

import numpy as np
import numpy.typing as npt

Array = npt.NDArray[Any]
Direction = Literal["higher", "lower"]
Settings = Mapping[str, int | float | str | bool]

EVAL_SEEDS: tuple[int, ...] = tuple(range(1_000_000, 1_000_020))
FINAL_SEEDS: tuple[int, ...] = tuple(range(2_000_000, 2_000_100))


def _same_fields(a: object, b: object) -> bool:
    """Field-by-field equality where array fields compare by dtype, shape and values."""
    for f in fields(a):  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        x, y = getattr(a, f.name), getattr(b, f.name)
        if isinstance(x, np.ndarray) or isinstance(y, np.ndarray):
            if not (
                isinstance(x, np.ndarray)
                and isinstance(y, np.ndarray)
                and x.dtype == y.dtype
                and np.array_equal(x, y)
            ):
                return False
        elif x != y:
            return False
    return True

"""The shared contract types: world and policy protocols, settings, seed sets and outputs."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Mapping
from dataclasses import dataclass, fields
from pathlib import Path
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Literal, Protocol

import numpy as np
import numpy.typing as npt

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from _typeshed import DataclassInstance

Array = npt.NDArray[Any]
Direction = Literal["higher", "lower"]
Settings = Mapping[str, int | float | str | bool]

EVAL_SEEDS: tuple[int, ...] = tuple(range(1_000_000, 1_000_020))
FINAL_SEEDS: tuple[int, ...] = tuple(range(2_000_000, 2_000_100))


def _same_fields(a: DataclassInstance, b: DataclassInstance) -> bool:
    """Field-by-field equality where array fields compare by dtype, shape and values."""
    for f in fields(a):
        x, y = getattr(a, f.name), getattr(b, f.name)
        if isinstance(x, np.ndarray) and isinstance(y, np.ndarray):
            if x.dtype != y.dtype or not np.array_equal(x, y):
                return False
        elif isinstance(x, np.ndarray) or isinstance(y, np.ndarray) or x != y:
            return False
    return True


class ActionError(ValueError):
    """An action outside the world's declared `ActionSpace`; never clipped."""

    def __init__(self, agent: str, value: object) -> None:
        super().__init__(f"agent {agent!r}: action {value!r} is outside the action space")
        self.agent = agent
        self.value = value


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Discrete:
    """Actions are ints in [0, n)."""

    n: int


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Box:
    """Actions are `dims` floats in [low, high]."""

    dims: int
    low: float
    high: float


ActionSpace = Discrete | Box


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TeamSpec:
    name: str
    agents: tuple[int, ...]
    score_name: str
    direction: Direction


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class MeasureSpec:
    name: str
    team: str
    direction: Direction


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class WorldSpec:
    world: str
    variant: str
    agents: tuple[str, ...]
    teams: tuple[TeamSpec, ...]
    obs_len: int
    action: ActionSpace
    max_steps: int
    measures: tuple[MeasureSpec, ...]
    sight: float | None


@dataclass(frozen=True, eq=False)
class Step:
    """`obs` float32 n_agents x obs_len; `rewards` float32 n_agents; `active` bool n_agents."""

    obs: Array
    rewards: Array
    active: Array
    done: bool
    truncated: bool

    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
        if not isinstance(other, Step):
            return NotImplemented
        return _same_fields(self, other)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EpisodeResult:
    seed: int
    length: int
    scores: Mapping[str, float]
    team_rewards: Mapping[str, float]
    measures: Mapping[str, float]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Drawable:
    kind: str
    x: float
    y: float
    size: float
    team: str | None
    agent: int | None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DrawState:
    width: float
    height: float
    objects: tuple[Drawable, ...]


@dataclass(frozen=True, eq=False)
class Frame:
    step: int
    draw: DrawState
    scores: Mapping[str, float]
    rewards: Array

    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
        if not isinstance(other, Frame):
            return NotImplemented
        return _same_fields(self, other)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Episode:
    """`frames` is set only when traced, with `result.length + 1` entries."""

    result: EpisodeResult
    frames: tuple[Frame, ...] | None
    hit_step_limit: bool


class World(Protocol):
    spec: WorldSpec

    def reset(self, seed: int) -> Step: ...

    def step(self, actions: Array) -> Step: ...

    def result(self) -> EpisodeResult: ...

    def draw(self) -> DrawState: ...


class Policy(Protocol):
    def act(self, obs: Array, rng: np.random.Generator) -> Array: ...


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Output:
    path: Path
    kind: Literal["chart", "video", "writeup"]
    made_from: tuple[str, ...]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class MethodConfig:
    """Full method settings: missing keys are filled with the method's defaults (AD-12)."""

    method: Literal["dqn", "ppo"]
    settings: Settings


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RunConfig:
    """One run: `methods` has one entry per team; `budget` counts world steps (AD-12)."""

    name: str
    world: str
    variant: str
    methods: Mapping[str, MethodConfig]
    seed: int
    budget: int
    check_settings: Mapping[str, Settings]
    device: str = "cpu"

"""JSON form of the contract types, shared by run folders, checkpoints and contract samples.

`encode` turns a contract value into plain JSON data; `decode` turns it back, checking every field
against the type's annotations. Arrays are `{"dtype", "shape", "data"}`; paths and datetimes are
strings; a `timedelta` is seconds; a union of dataclasses is told apart by its keys.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import types
import typing
from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Literal, TypeVar, get_args, get_origin, get_type_hints

import numpy as np

T = TypeVar("T")
Json = None | bool | int | float | str | list["Json"] | dict[str, "Json"]


def encode(value: object) -> Json:
    """Plain JSON data for a contract value."""
    if isinstance(value, np.ndarray):
        return {"dtype": str(value.dtype), "shape": list(value.shape), "data": value.tolist()}
    if dataclasses.is_dataclass(value) and not isinstance(value, type):
        return {f.name: encode(getattr(value, f.name)) for f in dataclasses.fields(value)}
    if isinstance(value, Mapping):
        return {str(k): encode(v) for k, v in value.items()}
    if isinstance(value, tuple | list):
        return [encode(v) for v in value]
    return _encode_leaf(value)


def _encode_leaf(value: object) -> Json:
    if isinstance(value, np.generic):
        value = value.item()
    if value is None or isinstance(value, bool | int | float | str):
        return value
    if isinstance(value, timedelta):
        return value.total_seconds()
    if isinstance(value, datetime):
        return value.isoformat()
    if isinstance(value, Path):
        return value.as_posix()
    raise TypeError(f"no JSON form for {type(value).__name__}")


def decode(cls: type[T], data: object) -> T:
    """A `cls` value from JSON data; `TypeError` naming the first field that doesn't fit."""
    value = decode_hint(cls, data)
    if not isinstance(value, cls):
        raise TypeError(f"expected {cls.__name__}, got {type(value).__name__}")
    return value


def decode_hint(hint: object, data: object) -> object:
    """A value of any annotation (`ActionSpace`, `tuple[int, ...]`, ...) from JSON data."""
    if hint is Any or hint is object:
        return data
    handler = _HANDLERS.get(get_origin(hint) or hint)
    if handler is not None:
        return handler(hint, data)
    if isinstance(hint, type) and dataclasses.is_dataclass(hint):
        return _decode_dataclass(hint, data)
    leaf = _LEAVES.get(hint)
    if leaf is None:
        raise TypeError(f"no JSON form for {hint!r}")
    return leaf(data)


def _decode_dataclass(cls: type[Any], data: object) -> object:
    obj = _as_dict(data)
    hints = get_type_hints(cls)
    names = {f.name for f in dataclasses.fields(cls)}
    unknown = sorted(set(obj) - names)
    if unknown:
        raise TypeError(f"{cls.__name__}: unknown fields {unknown}")
    try:
        kwargs = {k: decode_hint(hints[k], v) for k, v in obj.items()}
    except TypeError as exc:
        raise TypeError(f"{cls.__name__}.{exc}") from exc
    return cls(**kwargs)


def _decode_union(hint: object, data: object) -> object:
    errors = []
    for option in get_args(hint):
        try:
            return decode_hint(option, data)
        except TypeError as exc:
            errors.append(str(exc))
    raise TypeError(f"{data!r} fits none of {hint!r}: {errors}")


def _decode_literal(hint: object, data: object) -> object:
    if data not in get_args(hint):
        raise TypeError(f"{data!r} is not one of {get_args(hint)}")
    return data


def _decode_array(_hint: object, data: object) -> object:
    obj = _as_dict(data)
    if set(obj) != {"dtype", "shape", "data"}:
        raise TypeError(f"an array needs dtype, shape and data, got {sorted(obj)}")
    shape = decode_hint(tuple[int, ...], obj["shape"])
    return np.asarray(obj["data"], dtype=np.dtype(_as_str(obj["dtype"]))).reshape(shape)


def _decode_tuple(hint: object, data: object) -> object:
    if not isinstance(data, list):
        raise TypeError(f"expected a list, got {data!r}")
    args = get_args(hint)
    if len(args) == 2 and args[1] is Ellipsis:
        return tuple(decode_hint(args[0], v) for v in data)
    if len(args) != len(data):
        raise TypeError(f"expected {len(args)} items, got {len(data)}")
    return tuple(decode_hint(a, v) for a, v in zip(args, data, strict=True))


def _decode_mapping(hint: object, data: object) -> object:
    _key, value_hint = get_args(hint)
    return {k: decode_hint(value_hint, v) for k, v in _as_dict(data).items()}


def _as_dict(data: object) -> dict[str, object]:
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise TypeError(f"expected an object, got {data!r}")
    return {_as_str(k): v for k, v in data.items()}


def _as_str(data: object) -> str:
    if not isinstance(data, str):
        raise TypeError(f"expected a string, got {data!r}")
    return data


def _as_none(data: object) -> None:
    if data is not None:
        raise TypeError(f"expected null, got {data!r}")


def _as_bool(data: object) -> bool:
    if not isinstance(data, bool):
        raise TypeError(f"expected a boolean, got {data!r}")
    return data


def _as_int(data: object) -> int:
    if isinstance(data, bool) or not isinstance(data, int):
        raise TypeError(f"expected an integer, got {data!r}")
    return data


def _as_float(data: object) -> float:
    if isinstance(data, bool) or not isinstance(data, int | float):
        raise TypeError(f"expected a number, got {data!r}")
    return float(data)


_HANDLERS: dict[object, Callable[[object, object], object]] = {
    typing.Union: _decode_union,
    types.UnionType: _decode_union,
    Literal: _decode_literal,
    np.ndarray: _decode_array,
    tuple: _decode_tuple,
    Mapping: _decode_mapping,
    dict: _decode_mapping,
}
_LEAVES: dict[object, Callable[[object], object]] = {
    type(None): _as_none,
    bool: _as_bool,
    int: _as_int,
    float: _as_float,
    str: _as_str,
    Path: lambda data: Path(_as_str(data)),
    datetime: lambda data: datetime.fromisoformat(_as_str(data)),
    timedelta: lambda data: timedelta(seconds=_as_float(data)),
}

"""methods contract types: the learner protocol, its transitions and its errors."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, fields
from typing import Protocol

import numpy as np

from rllab.core import Array, Policy


class NonFiniteError(ArithmeticError):
    """A loss or parameter became NaN or infinite; raised before any parameter changes."""

    def __init__(self, value: float) -> None:
        super().__init__(f"non-finite value {value}")
        self.value = value


class SpecMismatchError(ValueError):
    """A checkpoint's world spec no longer matches the world; names each differing field."""

    def __init__(self, fields: tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
        super().__init__(f"checkpoint spec differs from the world in: {', '.join(fields)}")
        self.fields = fields


@dataclass(frozen=True, eq=False)
class Transition:
    """One world step for one team: rows are the team's agents in `TeamSpec.agents` order."""

    obs: Array
    actions: Array
    rewards: Array
    next_obs: Array
    done: bool
    truncated: bool
    active: Array

    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
        if not isinstance(other, Transition):
            return NotImplemented
        return all(
            np.array_equal(getattr(self, f.name), getattr(other, f.name)) for f in fields(self)
        )

    def __hash__(self) -> int:
        return hash(tuple(np.asarray(getattr(self, f.name)).tobytes() for f in fields(self)))


class Learner(Protocol):
    """A hand-written learner for one team (CHECK-01)."""

    def act(self, obs: Array, rng: np.random.Generator) -> Array:
        """Exploring actions for the team's agents."""
        ...

    def observe(self, t: Transition) -> None:
        """Learn from one transition, on the learner's own schedule; `NonFiniteError` on NaN."""
        ...

    def policy(self) -> Policy:
        """A frozen, deterministic copy: greedy (DQN) or the mean action (PPO)."""
        ...

    def state_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]: ...

"""runlog contract types: run records, evaluation points, checkpoints and run views.

Every field type comes from `core`, so `runlog` imports `core` only (AD-12).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Mapping
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal, Protocol

from rllab.core import EpisodeResult, MethodConfig, RunConfig, WorldSpec

RunStatus = Literal["running", "finished", "incomplete", "failed"]


class RunExistsError(FileExistsError):
    """The run folder already exists; nothing was written."""

    def __init__(self, path: Path) -> None:
        super().__init__(f"run folder {path} already exists")
        self.path = path


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Failure:
    """Where a run stopped on a non-finite value, and its last good checkpoint."""

    step: int
    value: float
    checkpoint: Path


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RunRecord:
    """The LOG-01 record; `config.methods` holds full settings, defaults included."""

    config: RunConfig
    spec: WorldSpec
    started: datetime
    ended: datetime | None
    status: RunStatus
    failure: Failure | None
    path: Path


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EvalPoint:
    """Means over the 20 `EVAL_SEEDS` episodes, per team and per measure."""

    step: int
    scores: Mapping[str, float]
    measures: Mapping[str, float]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Checkpoint:
    """`pct` in {0, 10, ..., 100}; `state` keyed by team."""

    run: str
    pct: int
    step: int
    spec: WorldSpec
    methods: Mapping[str, MethodConfig]
    state: Mapping[str, dict[str, object]]
    path: Path


class Run(Protocol):
    """A read-only view of one run folder, readable while the run writes (LOG-06)."""

    record: RunRecord

    def episodes(self) -> list[EpisodeResult]: ...

    def evals(self) -> list[EvalPoint]: ...

    def checkpoints(self) -> list[Checkpoint]: ...


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Progress:
    """A live snapshot of a run, at most one evaluation point behind it."""

    step: int
    budget: int
    latest: EvalPoint | None
    elapsed: timedelta
    status: str

"""train contract types: the method check's result and the batch refusal."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CheckResult:
    """`agreement` is the share of check-world states where the trained policy picks the best
    action; `passed` is `agreement >= 0.95` (TRAIN-06)."""

    method: str
    world: str
    agreement: float
    passed: bool


class CheckFailedError(RuntimeError):
    """A method failed its check world, so the batch was refused before any run started."""

    def __init__(self, result: CheckResult) -> None:
        super().__init__(
            f"method {result.method!r} failed its check on {result.world!r}: "
            f"agreement {result.agreement:.2f} < 0.95"
        )
        self.result = result

"""evaluate contract types: baseline comparisons, verdicts and per-team summaries."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Mapping
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Literal


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Comparison:
    """One EVAL-04 test; `difference` is positive when the learned agent is better."""

    baseline: Literal["random", "rule"]
    team: str
    learned_mean: float
    baseline_mean: float
    difference: float
    p_raw: float
    p_holm: float
    rejected: bool


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Verdict:
    """The EVAL-05 verdict; `runs_needed` > 0 when there were fewer than 5 runs."""

    beats_baselines: bool
    failing_runs: tuple[str, ...]
    runs_needed: int


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Summary:
    """The EVAL-06 summary of one world, variant and team."""

    world: str
    variant: str
    team: str
    runs: tuple[str, ...]
    learned_mean: float
    learned_range: tuple[float, float]
    run_means: Mapping[str, float]
    random_mean: float
    rule_mean: float
    comparisons: tuple[Comparison, ...]
    verdict: Verdict
    collapse: int | None

"""The `rllab` command: each trigger dispatched to its pipeline entry, its result printed (AD-10).

`--smoke` on a subcommand runs that pipeline end to end on its small built-in input, writing into
a temporary folder.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from collections.abc import Callable, Sequence
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

from rllab.cli.pipelines import pl04_watch, pl05_chart, pl06_evaluate
from rllab.train import run_batch, run_check
from rllab.train.pipelines import pl01_check, pl02_train, pl03_batch

# The arguments each subcommand needs unless it runs with --smoke.
REQUIRED = {
    "check": ("config",),
    "train": ("config", "seed"),
    "batch": ("config", "seeds"),
    "watch": ("run_path",),
    "chart": ("world", "variant"),
    "evaluate": ("world", "variant"),
}


def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Run one subcommand; print its result, or its error as one line with exit code 1."""
    parser = _parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    missing = [name for name in REQUIRED[args.command] if getattr(args, name) is None]
    if missing and not args.smoke:
        parser.error(f"{args.command} needs {', '.join(missing)} (or --smoke)")
    try:
        result = args.run(args)
    except Exception as exc:  # every error is reported as one line naming its cause
        print(f"rllab {args.command}: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    for item in result if isinstance(result, list) else [result]:
        print(item)
    return 0


def _check(args: argparse.Namespace) -> object:
    if args.smoke:
        return pl01_check.smoke()
    return run_check(args.config, args.seed or 0)


def _train(args: argparse.Namespace) -> object:
    if args.smoke:
        return _in_temp_folder(pl02_train.smoke)
    return run_batch(args.config, [args.seed], args.root, workers=1)


def _batch(args: argparse.Namespace) -> object:
    if args.smoke:
        return _in_temp_folder(pl03_batch.smoke)
    return run_batch(
        args.config, args.seeds, args.root, workers=args.workers, check_seed=args.check_seed
    )


def _watch(args: argparse.Namespace) -> object:
    if args.smoke:
        return pl04_watch.smoke()
    return pl04_watch.run_watch(args.run_path)


def _chart(args: argparse.Namespace) -> object:
    if args.smoke:
        return _in_temp_folder(pl05_chart.smoke)
    return pl05_chart.run_chart(
        args.root, args.world, args.variant, include=args.include, measure=args.measure
    )


def _evaluate(args: argparse.Namespace) -> object:
    if args.smoke:
        return _in_temp_folder(pl06_evaluate.smoke)
    today = datetime.now(UTC).astimezone().date().isoformat()
    out = args.out or args.root / args.world / args.variant / "_eval" / today
    return pl06_evaluate.run_evaluate(args.root, args.world, args.variant, out, include=args.include)


def _in_temp_folder(smoke: Callable[[Path], object]) -> object:
    with TemporaryDirectory(prefix="rllab-smoke-") as tmp:
        return smoke(Path(tmp))


def _seeds(text: str) -> list[int]:
    """`1-5` or `1,3,5` as a list of seeds."""
    if "-" in text:
        first, last = text.split("-", 1)
        return list(range(int(first), int(last) + 1))
    return [int(part) for part in text.split(",")]


def _parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="rllab", description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    def command(name: str, run: Callable[[argparse.Namespace], object]) -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
        sub = commands.add_parser(name)
        sub.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true", help="run on the built-in smoke input")
        sub.set_defaults(run=run)
        return sub

    check = command("check", _check)
    check.add_argument("config", type=Path, nargs="?")
    check.add_argument("--seed", type=int)
    train = command("train", _train)
    train.add_argument("config", type=Path, nargs="?")
    train.add_argument("--seed", type=int)
    train.add_argument("--root", type=Path, default=Path("runs"))
    batch = command("batch", _batch)
    batch.add_argument("config", type=Path, nargs="?")
    batch.add_argument("--seeds", type=_seeds)
    batch.add_argument("--root", type=Path, default=Path("runs"))
    batch.add_argument("--workers", type=int)
    batch.add_argument("--check-seed", type=int, default=0)

"""The `rllab` command: each trigger dispatched to its pipeline entry, its result printed (AD-10).

`--smoke` on a subcommand runs that pipeline end to end on its small built-in input, writing into
a temporary folder.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from collections.abc import Callable, Sequence
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

from rllab.cli.pipelines import pl04_watch, pl05_chart, pl06_evaluate
from rllab.train import run_batch, run_check
from rllab.train.pipelines import pl01_check, pl02_train, pl03_batch

# The arguments each subcommand needs unless it runs with --smoke.
REQUIRED = {
    "check": ("config",),
    "train": ("config", "seed"),
    "batch": ("config", "seeds"),
    "watch": ("run_path",),
    "chart": ("world", "variant"),
    "evaluate": ("world", "variant"),
}


def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Run one subcommand; print its result, or its error as one line with exit code 1."""
    parser = _parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    missing = [name for name in REQUIRED[args.command] if getattr(args, name) is None]
    if missing and not args.smoke:
        parser.error(f"{args.command} needs {', '.join(missing)} (or --smoke)")
    try:
        result = args.run(args)
    except Exception as exc:  # every error is reported as one line naming its cause
        print(f"rllab {args.command}: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    for item in result if isinstance(result, list) else [result]:
        print(item)
    return 0


def _check(args: argparse.Namespace) -> object:
    if args.smoke:
        return pl01_check.smoke()
    return run_check(args.config, args.seed)


def _train(args: argparse.Namespace) -> object:
    if args.smoke:
        return _in_temp_folder(pl02_train.smoke)
    return run_batch(args.config, [args.seed], args.root, workers=1)


def _batch(args: argparse.Namespace) -> object:
    if args.smoke:
        return _in_temp_folder(pl03_batch.smoke)
    return run_batch(
        args.config, args.seeds, args.root, workers=args.workers, check_seed=args.check_seed
    )


def _watch(args: argparse.Namespace) -> object:
    if args.smoke:
        return pl04_watch.smoke()
    return pl04_watch.run_watch(args.run_path)


def _chart(args: argparse.Namespace) -> object:
    if args.smoke:
        return _in_temp_folder(pl05_chart.smoke)
    return pl05_chart.run_chart(
        args.root, args.world, args.variant, include=args.include, measure=args.measure
    )


def _evaluate(args: argparse.Namespace) -> object:
    if args.smoke:
        return _in_temp_folder(pl06_evaluate.smoke)
    today = datetime.now(UTC).astimezone().date().isoformat()
    out = args.out or args.root / args.world / args.variant / "_eval" / today
    return pl06_evaluate.run_evaluate(
        args.root, args.world, args.variant, out, include=args.include
    )


def _in_temp_folder(smoke: Callable[[Path], object]) -> object:
    with TemporaryDirectory(prefix="rllab-smoke-") as tmp:
        return smoke(Path(tmp))


def seeds_arg(text: str) -> list[int]:
    """`1-5` or `1,3,5` as a list of seeds."""
    if "-" in text:
        first, last = text.split("-", 1)
        return list(range(int(first), int(last) + 1))
    return [int(part) for part in text.split(",")]


def _parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="rllab", description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    def command(name: str, run: Callable[[argparse.Namespace], object]) -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
        sub = commands.add_parser(name)
        sub.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true", help="run on the built-in smoke input")
        sub.set_defaults(run=run)
        return sub

    check = command("check", _check)
    check.add_argument("config", type=Path, nargs="?")
    check.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
    train = command("train", _train)
    train.add_argument("config", type=Path, nargs="?")
    train.add_argument("--seed", type=int)
    train.add_argument("--root", type=Path, default=Path("runs"))
    batch = command("batch", _batch)
    batch.add_argument("config", type=Path, nargs="?")
    batch.add_argument("--seeds", type=seeds_arg)
    batch.add_argument("--root", type=Path, default=Path("runs"))
    batch.add_argument("--workers", type=int)
    batch.add_argument("--check-seed", type=int, default=0)
    watch = command("watch", _watch)
    watch.add_argument("run_path", type=Path, nargs="?")
    for name, run in (("chart", _chart), ("evaluate", _evaluate)):
        sub = command(name, run)
        sub.add_argument("world", nargs="?")
        sub.add_argument("variant", nargs="?")
        sub.add_argument("--include", action="append", default=[])
        sub.add_argument("--root", type=Path, default=Path("runs"))
        if name == "chart":
            sub.add_argument("--measure")
        else:
            sub.add_argument("--out", type=Path)
    return parser

"""Loaders for the frozen boundary contracts in this folder (CR-09).

Each `tests/contracts/<component>.<symbol>/` folder holds a `schema.json` (JSON Schema), one
`samples/<case>.json` per contract case, and, for a Protocol or class, a `double.py` replaying its
recording, or, for a boundary function, a `fake.py` serving its fixtures.

A test outside this folder loads the kit by path, since the folder is not a package:

    import runpy
    from pathlib import Path

    KIT = runpy.run_path(str(Path(__file__).parents[2] / "contracts" / "kit.py"))
    world = KIT["double"]("core.World", "snake-seed42")
    spec = KIT["sample"](WorldSpec, "core.WorldSpec", "snake")
    make = KIT["fake"]("worlds.make")
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import json
import sys
from collections.abc import Callable
from pathlib import Path
from types import ModuleType
from typing import Any

from rllab.core.codec import decode

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent


def folder(symbol: str) -> Path:
    """The contract folder of `symbol`, e.g. `core.World`."""
    path = ROOT / symbol
    if not path.is_dir():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no contract folder for {symbol}")
    return path


def symbols() -> list[str]:
    """Every contract folder's symbol."""
    return sorted(p.name for p in ROOT.iterdir() if p.is_dir() and "." in p.name)


def cases(symbol: str) -> list[str]:
    """The case names of `symbol`'s samples."""
    return sorted(p.stem for p in (folder(symbol) / "samples").glob("*.json"))


def load(symbol: str, case: str) -> Any:
    """One sample as plain JSON data."""
    return json.loads((folder(symbol) / "samples" / f"{case}.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def schema(symbol: str) -> Any:
    return json.loads((folder(symbol) / "schema.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def sample[T](cls: type[T], symbol: str, case: str) -> T:
    """One sample decoded into its contract type."""
    return decode(cls, load(symbol, case))


def module(symbol: str, name: str) -> ModuleType:
    """The folder's `double.py` or `fake.py`, imported once by path."""
    key = f"contracts.{symbol.replace('.', '_')}.{name}"
    if key not in sys.modules:
        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(key, folder(symbol) / f"{name}.py")
        if spec is None or spec.loader is None:
            raise ImportError(f"cannot load {name}.py for {symbol}")
        mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
        sys.modules[key] = mod
        spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
    return sys.modules[key]


def double(symbol: str, case: str) -> Any:
    """The replay double of a Protocol or class, serving the recording `case`."""
    return module(symbol, "double").load(case)


def fake(symbol: str) -> Callable[..., Any]:
    """The fake of a boundary function, with the function's own signature."""
    return getattr(module(symbol, "fake"), symbol.split(".")[-1])


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------- JSON Schema subset
# Enough of JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for these folders: type, enum, const, properties,
# required, additionalProperties, items, prefixItems, minItems, maxItems, minimum, maximum,
# anyOf and local $ref into $defs.
_TYPES: dict[str, Callable[[object], bool]] = {
    "object": lambda v: isinstance(v, dict),
    "array": lambda v: isinstance(v, list),
    "string": lambda v: isinstance(v, str),
    "integer": lambda v: isinstance(v, int) and not isinstance(v, bool),
    "number": lambda v: isinstance(v, int | float) and not isinstance(v, bool),
    "boolean": lambda v: isinstance(v, bool),
    "null": lambda v: v is None,
}


def validate(data: object, rules: dict[str, Any], root: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> list[str]:
    """Every way `data` breaks `rules`, as `$.path: problem` lines; empty when valid."""
    return _check(data, rules, root or rules, "$")


def _check(data: object, rules: dict[str, Any], root: dict[str, Any], at: str) -> list[str]:
    if "$ref" in rules:
        name = rules["$ref"].removeprefix("#/$defs/")
        return _check(data, root["$defs"][name], root, at)
    if "anyOf" in rules:
        if any(not _check(data, option, root, at) for option in rules["anyOf"]):
            return []
        return [f"{at}: matches none of anyOf"]
    errors = _check_scalar(data, rules, at)
    if errors:
        return errors
    if isinstance(data, dict):
        return _check_object(data, rules, root, at)
    if isinstance(data, list):
        return _check_array(data, rules, root, at)
    return []


def _check_scalar(data: object, rules: dict[str, Any], at: str) -> list[str]:
    kinds = rules.get("type")
    kinds = [kinds] if isinstance(kinds, str) else kinds
    if kinds and not any(_TYPES[k](data) for k in kinds):
        return [f"{at}: expected {'/'.join(kinds)}, got {data!r}"]
    if "enum" in rules and data not in rules["enum"]:
        return [f"{at}: {data!r} not in {rules['enum']}"]
    if "const" in rules and data != rules["const"]:
        return [f"{at}: expected {rules['const']!r}"]
    if isinstance(data, int | float) and not isinstance(data, bool):
        if "minimum" in rules and data < rules["minimum"]:
            return [f"{at}: {data} < {rules['minimum']}"]
        if "maximum" in rules and data > rules["maximum"]:
            return [f"{at}: {data} > {rules['maximum']}"]
    return []


def _check_object(
    data: dict[str, Any], rules: dict[str, Any], root: dict[str, Any], at: str
) -> list[str]:
    props = rules.get("properties", {})
    errors = [f"{at}: missing {k!r}" for k in rules.get("required", []) if k not in data]
    extra = rules.get("additionalProperties", True)
    for key, value in data.items():
        if key in props:
            errors += _check(value, props[key], root, f"{at}.{key}")
        elif extra is False:
            errors.append(f"{at}: unexpected {key!r}")
        elif isinstance(extra, dict):
            errors += _check(value, extra, root, f"{at}.{key}")
    return errors


def _check_array(data: list[Any], rules: dict[str, Any], root: dict[str, Any], at: str) -> list[str]:
    errors = []
    if len(data) < rules.get("minItems", 0):
        errors.append(f"{at}: fewer than {rules['minItems']} items")
    if "maxItems" in rules and len(data) > rules["maxItems"]:
        errors.append(f"{at}: more than {rules['maxItems']} items")
    prefix = rules.get("prefixItems", [])
    for i, value in enumerate(data):
        item = prefix[i] if i < len(prefix) else rules.get("items")
        if isinstance(item, dict):
            errors += _check(value, item, root, f"{at}[{i}]")
    return errors

new
def _check(data: object, rules: dict[str, Any], root: dict[str, Any], at: str) -> list[str]:
    if "$ref" in rules:
        rules = root["$defs"][rules["$ref"].removeprefix("#/$defs/")]
        return _check(data, rules, root, at)
    if "anyOf" in rules:
        fits = any(not _check(data, option, root, at) for option in rules["anyOf"])
        return [] if fits else [f"{at}: matches none of anyOf"]
    errors = _check_scalar(data, rules, at)
    if not errors and isinstance(data, dict):
        errors = _check_object(data, rules, root, at)
    elif not errors and isinstance(data, list):
        errors = _check_array(data, rules, root, at)
    return errors


def _check_scalar(data: object, rules: dict[str, Any], at: str) -> list[str]:
    kinds = rules.get("type")
    kinds = [kinds] if isinstance(kinds, str) else kinds
    number = isinstance(data, int | float) and not isinstance(data, bool)
    problems = [
        (bool(kinds) and not any(_TYPES[k](data) for k in kinds), f"expected {kinds}"),
        ("enum" in rules and data not in rules["enum"], f"not in {rules.get('enum')}"),
        ("const" in rules and data != rules.get("const"), f"expected {rules.get('const')!r}"),
        (number and data < rules.get("minimum", data), f"below {rules.get('minimum')}"),
        (number and data > rules.get("maximum", data), f"above {rules.get('maximum')}"),
    ]
    return [f"{at}: {data!r} {message}" for broken, message in problems if broken][:1]
